messages.content: Help me signal the end of an XML element with the qualified name `{namespaceURI='http://www.example.com', localPart='item', prefix='ex'}` and augmentation information `augmentations` in an XML processing application that uses namespaces?

function.name: XMLNamespaceBinder_endElement
function.description: Signals the end of an XML element, handling namespace-related processing if namespaces are enabled, or delegating to the document handler otherwise. Note that the provided function is in Java 8 SDK syntax.

element.description: The qualified name of the element that is ending. Use QName object, has a constructor that takes in three parameters, namespaceURI, localPart, prefix This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

augs.description: Augmentation information associated with the element. This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

message.reasoning:
We need to call the tool functions.XMLNamespaceBinder_endElement with appropriate arguments.

The element argument should be a QName constructed from namespaceURI, localPart, prefix. In this context we just pass as string representation maybe "QName('http://www.example.com','item','ex')" but likely they want JSON-like structure: {namespaceURI:'...',localPart:'...'} etc. But spec says element param can be any type of Java object in string representation. So we could provide something like "new javax.xml.namespace.QName(\"http://www.example.com\", \"item\", \"ex\")". Let's do that.

Also augmentations param is string representation; we have variable named augmentations. We'll use it directly.

Thus produce:

{
"element":"javax.xml.namespace.QName{uri:http://www.example.com,name:item,prefix:ex}",
"augs":augmentations
}

But better to follow example: element: new QName("http://www.example.com","item","ex") . Provide as string.

Let's craft output accordingly.
